concepts.anchor: - Credits and prepaid commits draw down before postpaid commits; lower numeric priorities consume first.
concepts.proposed_markdown:
> [!warning] Contradiction
> The broad prepaid-before-postpaid rule has a rollover exception: the prioritization guide places postpaid rollover commits before prepaid rollover commits and credits. After the rollover tier, prepaid commits and credits still precede ordinary postpaid commits regardless of priority. Commit type outranks priority; same-type rollover ties use priority, narrower product applicability, narrower usage applicability, then earlier `ending_before`. Prepaid ties additionally place zero-dollar cost basis before paid value, then use earlier `starting_on` and fewer applicable contracts. The postpaid section says it follows prepaid logic but its abbreviated list omits usage applicability, so that tie-breaker remains ambiguous for postpaid commits.
warnings: This update must qualify the existing broad concept bullet and the related create-a-pre-paid-commit source summary; do not erase the ordinary prepaid-before-postpaid rule.
Do not infer that usage applicability is absent from postpaid ordering: the raw page says postpaid follows the same prepaid logic but omits that step from its abbreviated list.

concepts.anchor: Credits and commits apply at invoice line-item level.
concepts.proposed_markdown: When several eligible invoice lines can receive a credit or commit, Metronome applies the balance to usage products before subscription products and then composite products. Ties within a product type go to the earlier line-item start date, then the higher unit price, then alphabetical line-item name.
